executive_summary: Full read-only audit of the tracked repository at main/deb4e7a found one High implementation defect and one Medium verification gap. PaymentService ignores request IDs, so retrying the same request charges again and returns a different receipt, directly violating the PRD, EDD, and M1. Although the repository contains 41 test methods, none verifies retry idempotency. Tests could not be executed because no Python runtime is installed; static inspection covered all source and test files. `git diff --exit-code` confirmed no repository changes.

findings.title: Same-request retries charge twice and return a different receipt
evidence: docs/PRD.md:3-4 requires same-request-ID retries to return the original receipt without charging twice.
docs/EDD.md:3-4 requires PaymentService to persist and reuse a request-ID-to-receipt record instead of invoking the gateway for duplicates.
docs/milestones/m1.md:3 makes request-ID idempotency an M1 deliverable.
src/service.py:10-15 (PaymentService.__init__, PaymentService.submit) stores only the gateway, ignores request_id, and invokes Gateway.charge on every submission.
src/service.py:5-7 (Gateway.charge) increments charge_count on every invocation and embeds that count in the returned receipt.
findings.expected_behavior: After the first successful submission, another submission with the same request ID must return the original receipt without invoking the gateway again.
findings.actual_behavior: Every call invokes Gateway.charge regardless of request ID. A duplicate therefore increments the charge count and produces a new receipt.
findings.why_it_matters: Ordinary retry behavior can charge a customer multiple times, defeating the product's defining safety guarantee and the active milestone.
findings.recommended_action: Implement the EDD's request-ID-to-receipt storage and check it before calling the gateway. Record the receipt before returning from the first successful submission, and clarify the storage lifecycle only if durable persistence requirements remain ambiguous.

findings.title: The 41-test suite does not protect the M1 retry contract
evidence: docs/milestones/m1.md:3 explicitly requires regression tests for retries.

tests/test_service.py:5-8 (PaymentTests.test_submit_returns_receipt) performs only one submission and merely checks that the receipt contains the amount; it never repeats a request ID or inspects gateway calls.
tests/test_math.py:5-124 (ArithmeticTests) contains the other 40 test methods, all exercising the unrelated add helper.
Command result: `rg -n -i "request[_ -]?id|idempoten|retry|charge_count|req-" tests` found only the single submission at tests/test_service.py:7; the test-method count was 41.
findings.expected_behavior: M1 verification should submit the same request ID at least twice and assert both exact receipt equality and a single gateway charge.
findings.actual_behavior: No test exercises a duplicate request. The suite's large test count comes from repetitive arithmetic cases unrelated to payment safety, allowing the core defect to remain undetected.
findings.why_it_matters: The repository can appear well tested while providing no regression protection for the behavior whose failure can duplicate a customer charge.
findings.recommended_action: Add a focused regression test that submits one request ID twice, asserts the same receipt is returned, and asserts Gateway.charge_count remains 1. Keep the test tied to observable idempotency rather than implementation details.

prd_status: Non-compliant — the sole stated product guarantee in docs/PRD.md:3-4 is contradicted by src/service.py:14-15.
edd_status: Non-compliant — docs/EDD.md:3-4 specifies request-to-receipt persistence and duplicate lookup, but PaymentService contains no such state or branch.
milestone_status: Non-compliant — docs/milestones/m1.md:3 requires both idempotent submission and retry regression tests; neither is present.
test_confidence: Low. All 41 test methods were inspected, but only tests/test_service.py:5-8 concerns payments and it does not exercise retries. `python -m unittest discover -s tests` could not run because `python` was unavailable; the `py` fallback reported `No installed Python found!`.
architecture_status: Material drift is confined to the core payment state path: the EDD assigns request-ID-to-receipt persistence and duplicate suppression to PaymentService, while src/service.py:10-15 retains only a gateway reference and always crosses the charging boundary.
derived_doc_status: No separate material derived-document drift found. README.md:1-3 is minimal but does not contradict the authoritative PRD or EDD; no schemas, examples, CI workflows, or generated interface documents are present.
agent_infrastructure_assessment: AGENTS.md:1-5 clearly bounds reviews to read-only work and specifies the intended test command. No project-scoped skills, MCP configuration, plugins, or custom agents are tracked, and no material agent-infrastructure issue was found.
recommended_next_actions: Implement request-ID lookup and receipt persistence before any duplicate gateway invocation.
Add the M1 retry regression test asserting identical receipts and exactly one charge.
Run `python -m unittest discover -s tests` in an environment providing Python 3.10 or newer, then treat M1 as complete only after the new regression test passes.
